entries.title: Independent dynamic checker disagrees with the maker on the frozen R13 candidate
entries.first_broken_link: checker (openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, isolated copy + own runtime) reports 8 passed / 1 failed: test_admission_fails_closed_when_target_is_not_a_repo DID NOT RAISE; the same copy run by the maker passed 9
entries.repair_cone: re-run the failing case under the checker runtime with -x --tb=long; if the import resolves to HG-KSEOS/src instead of the copy, pin PYTHONPATH/rootdir; until resolved the R13 static PASS is NOT dynamically confirmed
entries.resolution: The checker's FAIL was valid signal: the negative control was environment-dependent (under the lane sandbox TMPDIR sits inside the workspace, so the 'plain directory' target was itself inside a repository and rev-parse HEAD succeeded). Its first remedy - a hard refusal - was rejected by the oracle: 9 lifecycle tests use repo-relative targets, and the suite went 15F -> 24F. The check was reverted and the contract is now pinned by an environment-independent test that asserts a nested project records the TARGET repo's base_head and never the CWD's. Verified both ways.

entries.title: The far_lane_fix reds were a STALE CODEX TOOLCHAIN PIN, not an owner oracle
entries.first_broken_link: TestP0PinAssert pins a registry/assignment digest that the R14 rebind necessarily changes; matrix_d M07/M08 pin require-arm semantics
entries.required_authority: owner decision to re-pin or to keep the old pin as a historical oracle
entries.repair_cone: decide whether the pin oracle moves with the mandate; if it does, update pin + evidence in one change, never silently
entries.resolution: Measured, not assumed: all five reds (P0 x2, P1 x3) read var/FAR-LANE-REUSE-RCA-20261015/sources/task_local_toolchain.json, which pinned codex 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 @ 9614f1d9... / sha e98c516f.... The installed binary is now 0.163.0-alpha.11 @ 6257d9e8... / sha 00c0f1e4..., so the verifier refused before mandate resolution. Re-measured and re-pinned (golden values only; no semantic change), updated the test's hard-coded expected sha, and the file went 5 failed -> 11 passed. This was environment drift, NOT an assertion on the old mandate - my R14 note said otherwise and was wrong.
entries.residual: What IS an owner decision: matrix_d M07/M08 and the dispatcher pre-spawn case. They expect exit 3 for a required arm that is absent from a fixture pool, while the dispatcher returns 4 with the typed code ERR_LANE_REQUIRED_ARM_ABSENT. Note the test itself asserts the mandated EXECUTE arm is opencode-go/minimax-m3.1-flash-free, i.e. the R14 mandate - so this is an exit-code contract question, not a mandate question.

entries.title: The lane oracle tests are not under version control in HG-KSEOS
entries.first_broken_link: tests/test_lane_guard.py, tests/test_execute_luna_route.py and tests/test_far_lane_fix_20261015.py are untracked, so 'git archive <sha>' - the frozen-candidate mechanism the checker uses - silently omits the very files that define the lane oracle
entries.required_authority: owner decision to track them (or to define the freeze as an explicit manifest)
entries.repair_cone: either commit the oracle tests or freeze with a manifest of the files actually exercised; never let a checker adjudicate against a candidate that is missing its oracle
entries.observed: git ls-files tests/test_lane_guard.py -> 0; the checker reported 'Available 3 files ... test_lane_guard.py missing'
entries.resolution: A 16,734-entry inventory classified every path by content, not by name: 252 genuine source files are now tracked (so 'git archive' freezes the superoracle they adjudicate), 15,989 artifact entries are excluded via 154 precise .git/info/exclude patterns (preimage kept), 9 scratch files quarantined, and the six inherited tracked diffs were preserved byte-for-byte in a baseline commit that claims no authorship.
